headline: Microsoft lays off 4,800 employees and sells four Xbox studios in major gaming restructure
summary: Today's cuts impact ~1,600 Xbox staff, with Double Fine, Compulsion Games, Ninja Theory, and Undead Labs spun off as part of a multi-year 'reset' for the gaming division.
details: Microsoft is initiating a significant restructuring, impacting 4,800 employees across the company, with over 30% of these job losses occurring within its Xbox division. This move also includes the sale or spin-off of four prominent game studios. Approximately 1,600 Xbox employees are affected by immediate role eliminations.

The cuts are part of a broader "Xbox reset" aiming to reduce 20% of Xbox jobs, totaling around 3,200 positions, by the end of the financial year in July 2027. This year-long restructuring process is described as challenging by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.

Double Fine and Compulsion Games are returning to their founders, Tim Schafer and Guillaume Provost, respectively, regaining their independence. Ninja Theory, known for "Hellblade," and Undead Labs, developers of "State of Decay," are also being sold, with agreements in place to ensure their key franchises continue.

Sharma acknowledged the pain these changes inflict on employees who have dedicated their creativity to Xbox, many joining through acquisitions. She emphasized that these decisions do not reflect on their talent or dedication, but are necessary for the company's strategic realignment.

Microsoft is also considering the sale or closure of another Xbox studio, Arkane Studios, which is currently working on the delayed and over-budget "Blade" project. Consultations with Arkane's Works Council in France are underway to review potential strategic options.

Other Xbox studios, particularly Bethesda, will also experience layoffs, though no publicly announced first-party games or projects are being cancelled. Additionally, "Minecraft" developer Mojang and "Candy Crush" creator King will now report directly to Asha Sharma as part of the organizational changes.

These cuts appear to reverse some smaller studio acquisitions made to bolster Xbox Game Pass, with Microsoft now focusing on bigger franchises rather than competing with indies. The company aims to help independent creators succeed through open development tools rather than direct ownership.

Sharma stated that Xbox found itself losing 64 cents for every dollar invested in smaller studios, concluding that it is "neither possible nor desirable to own every great independent studio" and that Xbox is "not the best home for every type of studio."

headline_marked: [[Nvidia's Kyber rack for Rubin Ultra reportedly delayed to 2028]], stopgap solution also axed
headline: Nvidia's Kyber rack for Rubin Ultra reportedly delayed to 2028, stopgap solution also axed
summary: Manufacturing challenges with a complex PCB midplane are cited as the cause, pushing the cabinet meant for 2027's Rubin Ultra GPUs into the following year. This leaves Nvidia without a proven solution for scaling Rubin Ultra in 2027.
details: Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack, intended for 2027's Rubin Ultra GPUs, is reportedly delayed by over 12 months, now expected in 2028. Analyst firm SemiAnalysis attributes the holdup to manufacturing challenges with a crucial PCB midplane. Additionally, Nvidia has reportedly canceled NVL72x2, a stopgap rack designed to provide customers with an interim solution.

The Kyber rack features an orthogonal backplane, a rigid board replacing traditional cable harnesses to connect compute and switch trays. This innovative design carries the all-copper NVLink fabric and supports liquid cooling, stacking 144 Rubin Ultra packages—double the density of current Oberon NVL72 racks.

The orthogonal backplane is an engineering marvel, described as three 26-layer sections laminated into a single 78-layer stack. With trace spacing at or below 25μm, it maintains signal integrity for 448 Gb/s-class signaling, a task that would otherwise require over 20,000 discrete cables.

The NVL72x2 stopgap solution, which would have combined two Oberon racks for Kyber-class density, was reportedly abandoned after major customers rejected the two-linked-cabinets-as-one-unit approach. Another configuration, NVL576, which uses co-packaged optics to link eight racks, is also expected to be delayed or ship in low volume.

These reported cancellations and delays leave Nvidia without a proven solution to expand the scale-up world size for Rubin Ultra in 2027. This means the largest single Rubin Ultra domain in 2027 may not exceed the capabilities already offered by the Oberon generation. This news follows a recent decision by Nvidia to reduce the Rubin Ultra GPU to a dual-chiplet part due to manufacturing concerns.

The reported delay specifically impacts the Rubin Ultra phase and its dedicated Kyber rack. Nvidia's 2026 Rubin GPUs, which are designed to utilize the existing Oberon rack, are not part of this reported delay. Nvidia has been contacted for comment on these developments.
